Once a coroutine has been awaited to completion (return or raise), awaiting it again raises RuntimeError('cannot reuse already awaited coroutine') instead of actually retrying, so any test requiring more than one attempt fails or raises the wrong exception.

controls.name: swallows_cancellation_returns_none

controls.description: Task-specific near-miss: wraps the task in asyncio.shield() before handing it to asyncio.wait_for. shield() exists precisely to protect an awaitable from being cancelled when the coroutine awaiting it is cancelled -- so on timeout, wait_for cancels only the shield's outer proxy future, and the shielded inner task is never cancelled and keeps running in the background.
